## Practice areas

- [Car, Truck & Rideshare Accidents](https://sweet-platypus-bc9aa4.netlify.app/authority-car-accident.html): New York is a no-fault state, but an injury meeting the serious-injury threshold in Insurance Law 5102(d) opens full damages including pain and suffering.
- [Construction & Labor Law](https://sweet-platypus-bc9aa4.netlify.app/authority-construction.html): Labor Law 240, the Scaffold Law, imposes absolute liability on owners and general contractors for gravity-related accidents, without proof of negligence.
- [Medical Malpractice](https://sweet-platypus-bc9aa4.netlify.app/authority-malpractice.html): Requires proof that care fell below the accepted standard and caused harm. New York places no cap on non-economic damages.
- [Wrongful Death](https://sweet-platypus-bc9aa4.netlify.app/authority-wrongful-death.html): Two years from the date of death under EPTL 5-4.1, with a survival action for pre-death pain and suffering running alongside.
- [Catastrophic Injuries](https://sweet-platypus-bc9aa4.netlify.app/authority-catastrophic.html): Spinal cord, brain injury, amputation and burns, costed across a full life expectancy with certified life-care planning and forensic economics.
- [Premises Liability](https://sweet-platypus-bc9aa4.netlify.app/authority-premises.html): Turns on notice. Under NYC Administrative Code 7-210 the abutting property owner, not the City, maintains the sidewalk.

## Key New York deadlines

- Most personal injury claims: 3 years (CPLR 214(5)).
- Medical malpractice: 2 years 6 months (CPLR 214-a).
- Wrongful death: 2 years from the date of death (EPTL 5-4.1).
- Any claim against New York City, the MTA or a municipality: Notice of Claim within 90 days (General Municipal Law 50-e), suit within 1 year 90 days.
- No-fault (PIP) benefits: application to your own insurer within 30 days (11 NYCRR 65-1.1).
